messages:
incident-bot: Canary health alert (wave=2) — canary failure detected for deployment v2.3.4 in us-west-2. 5xx rate = 6.8% (1m), probe_failures spike, latency p99 increased. No automatic rollback (policy=manual). grafana: https://grafana.redwood/internal/d/canary-wave2; logs: https://logs.redwood/canary/5867001234

alex.m: seeing the same on traces — a bunch of requests are failing inside the prefetch/KV path. kvcache prefetch stall + connection queue growth on node set g4-*-usw2. CPU not super high, but thread blocking spikes.

maya.p: paging oncall now. I'm heading in, will coordinate rollback/flag. Sam, can you prepare an isolate?

sam.k: copying. pre-checking runbook: confirm canary traffic gating flag and routing flag available. Preparing command: `curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN" https://api.redwood/flags/wave2-route -d '{\"value\":0}'`

priya.s: customer-impact note: support telemetry shows ~0.12% of customer requests failing, mostly short-text generation (<=128 tokens). Affected customers: small but rising errors, some timeouts in mobile clients. Logged in INC-2026-0458 for tracking.

alex.m: snippets from node logs (redacted):
```
2026-03-15T13:40:21Z prefetch: kv_get timeout after 120ms, inflight=32
2026-03-15T13:40:22Z queue: conn_wait length=48, accept_delay=210ms
2026-03-15T13:40:23Z gen: handler panic -> retry -> 5xx
```
Looks like a prefetch stall causing backpressure and thrashing. Could be new prefetch optimization in v2.3.4.

maya.p: decision: isolate wave2 from routing fanout and enable kill-mode for canary-prefetch. Sam, flip the isolate flag and then cut traffic. Alex/priya watch metrics.

sam.k: executing now — running routing flag cut and feature flag flip.
`> /ops feature-flag set canary_fanout_isolate true --who sam.k`
`> curl -X POST https://api.redwood/flags/wave2-route -H 'Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN' -d '{"value":0}'`

sam.k: responses: feature-flag: OK; route change: propagated to edge controllers (ack ids: e5f3b4). Took ~18s to propagate.

incident-bot: Action ack: `canary_fanout_isolate=true` (actor=sam.k) | route wave2 -> 0 (actor=sam.k) | timestamp=5867001260. Noting mitigation in audit logs.

priya.s: after isolate, customer-impact trend: 5xx dropped to 1.2% within 60s but some latency p99 still elevated. Support notified customers in affected cohort; asked to escalate if SLA breaches.

alex.m: recommend revert of v2.3.4 -> v2.3.3 for wave2. We should not reintroduce prefetch optimization until root-cause confirmed. Sam, can you kick rollback and coordinate with releases?

sam.k: initiating rollback for wave2 -> v2.3.3 via deploy tool: `releases rollback --wave 2 --to v2.3.3 --requester sam.k` — job queued (job id 67291). ETA ~90s for rollout to start.

incident-bot: Deploy job 67291 started, strategy=rolling, max_concurrent=3. Will post updates.

oncall-lead: I'm taking handoff for monitoring. Maya, Alex — leave any troubleshooting notes here. I'll keep the channel open for updates and customer updates to INC-2026-0458.

maya.p: note for postmortem: investigate kvcache prefetch change in v2.3.4, add a canary-level prefetch circuit breaker, add probe that exercises small token paths to catch this earlier.

alex.m: +1. Also add autoscale guard for conn_wait growth and a short-circuit in prefetch after Xms.

sam.k: rollback job succeeded (job id 67291 -> status=success) at 5867001290. Observed 5xx baseline back to ~0.4% and p99 slowly normalizing.

oncall-lead: closing mitigation loop — wave2 isolated and rolled back. Incident ticket INC-2026-0458 updated with actions: isolate flag, rollback, customer notifications. Maya/Alex assigned for RCA. Leaving monitoring with oncall for next 2 hours. If metrics re-escalate, re-open. :white_check_mark:
